reason: Capillary networks connect the outgoing and returning vessels and provide thin walls for exchange.

reason: The filled circuit now appears ready to connect to the beating heart.

effect: The heart completed the closed circulation, showing blood returning to the pump and serving multiple tissues.
reaction: The closed-loop diagram brings the separate pieces together clearly.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building the blood-filled circuit was most worthwhile: the exchange inset showed oxygen and nutrients leaving the blood while red cells remain inside, connecting the vessel structure to tissue needs.

leastWorthwhile.text: Trying to connect the heart to the empty vessel circuit was frustrating because the pieces appeared ready to connect, but the attempt gave no indication that blood had to be added first.

surprise.text: The red blood cells make ATP from sugar despite having no nucleus or mitochondria, unlike the muscle cells in the earlier history.

arbitrary.text: The requirement to fill the vessels before connecting the heart felt arbitrary; the failed attempt did not explain the required order.

continue.text: I would continue: the contrast between red blood cells and muscle cells, and the way circulation connects the parts, made me curious about how the remaining systems will support the body.
